text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, the six activities A33, A35, A36, A37, A38 and A39 each run in about 99 in 100 traces, up from about 49–52 in 100 before (for example A33 appears in 98 of 200 traces before versus 197 of 200 after, and A37 in 105 versus 199). [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]
- Before, A33/A35/A36 on the one hand and A37/A38/A39 on the other behaved as two mutually exclusive sets: each set appeared together in about 49–52 in 100 traces and was jointly absent in about half, while a pair taken from different sets co-occurred in only about 1–3 in 200 traces. In the later window, every pair within and across the two sets co-occurs in about 98–99 in 100 traces, with A33, A35 and A36 preceding A37, A38 and A39 in about 95–97 in 100 of those traces. [REL037, REL044, REL055, REL059, REL039, REL041, REL045, REL047, REL050, REL052]
- The block now sits between the early and the late activities: A30 precedes each of the six in about 95–98 in 100 traces (before about 47 in 100), A31 follows each of them in about 95–99 in 100 (before about 47–52 in 100), A47/A48 now come after the whole block rather than after one half or the other, and A14 precedes the block in about 95–99 in 100; A15 co-occurs with the block in about 99 in 100 traces but with roughly 41 in 100 interleaved or repeated rather than strictly earlier. Consistently, A30's mean relative position moved earlier (about 0.67 to 0.62) and A31's later (about 0.80 to 0.82). [REL013, REL019, REL025, REL027, REL030, REL031, REL034, REL036, REL042, REL048, REL053, REL057, POS003, POS004]
- Step distances confirm this placement: the gap from A30 to A37/A38/A39 and from A33/A35/A36 to A31 grew from typically 1–3 positions to 4–5, the pairs A33→A37 and A36→A37 went from about 1 in 200 traces to about 195 in 200 (at distances of 2–5 positions), and A30→A31 within five steps fell from 199 to 5 traces. [LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG013, LAG014]
- A04 is executed far less often: it appears in about 26 in 100 later traces versus about 59 in 100 before; its co-occurrence with A14, A15, A30, A31, A47 and A48 dropped from about 59 to about 26 in 100; A14 now routes to A15 in about 79 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (A14→A04 fell from about 57 to 12 in 100); and the adjacent pairs A04→A15 and A14→A04 within five steps fell from 113 and 114 to 27 and 33 traces. [OCC002, REL001, REL003, REL011, DIR004, LAG001, LAG002]
- A few rare activities became more common: A02, A08 and A10 rose from about 5–8 in 100 traces to about 18–23 in 100. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process was modified so that two previously alternative branches — one containing A33, A35 and A36, the other A37, A38 and A39, each chosen in roughly half of the cases and almost never together — are now executed in sequence within a single pass in nearly every case, sitting between the early activities (A14, A15, A30) and the late activities (A31, A47, A48), while A04, which previously followed A14 in a majority of traces, is now executed in only about 26 in 100 traces. The 109 evidence items are roughly ninety times the number expected for an unchanged process (about 1.17), so chance cannot explain the pattern as a whole; the support is direct rather than purely frequency-based, because relational and lag evidence shows the new order and placement (mutual exclusivity turning into near-universal ordered co-occurrence, and step distances stretching exactly where the block now sits), and it is consistent across the occurrence, routing, position, relation and lag indicators — which, however, read the same traces from different angles and are not independent confirmations. [REL037, REL039, REL045, REL050, REL013, REL025, REL031, REL042, OCC002, DIR004, LAG005, LAG008]

Two limitations remain. The windows are finite samples, and the evidence cannot rule out that a rare pre-existing variant containing the whole block (cross-set pairs did co-occur in about 1–3 of 200 earlier traces) simply became dominant — a shift in the mix of existing variants that would look identical to a structural modification at this sample size; the differences are larger than in about 199 of 200 random re-splits, but that only shows they are unusual, not which explanation holds. In addition, the order within each half of the block remains mixed (for example A33 precedes A35 in only about 46 in 100 later traces), so no single fixed sequence inside the block is established. [REL039, REL041, REL037]
